biography.arunachala: Drawn to the sacred hill Arunachala, he left home and spent years in deep meditation, living in caves and silence.
biography.early_life: Ramana Maharshi was born as Venkataraman Iyer. At age 16, he experienced a profound spiritual awakening after a near-death experience, realizing the Self as pure consciousness.
biography.legacy: Ramana Maharshi is revered as a modern sage of Advaita Vedanta. His teachings and ashram at Arunachala continue to inspire spiritual seekers worldwide. He attained Mahasamadhi in 1950.
biography.teaching: Ramana taught the path of Self-Inquiry (Atma-Vichara), guiding seekers to ask 'Who am I?' and realize their true nature. His presence radiated peace, and he often taught through silence.

keyteachings.description: Investigate the source of the 'I' thought to realize the Self
True teaching is beyond words; silence conveys the highest truth
Complete surrender to the Self or God leads to liberation

realization.event: Spontaneous awakening at age 16 after a near-death experience
realization.insight: Realized the Self as deathless, pure consciousness

philosophicalthemes: Self alone is real; ego is an illusion

timeline.event: Born in Tiruchuli, Tamil Nadu in 1879
At age 16, experienced ego-death and awakening
Moved to Arunachala Hill; lived in caves in deep meditation
Taught Self-Inquiry through silence and brief instructions
Established Ramanashram; continued guiding seekers until Mahasamadhi in 1950
